newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Bundesbank leaves interest rates steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bundesbank leaves interest rates steady.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.

The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also left at a fixed three percent for the next two weeks.
Few economists had expected the German central bank to take action on rates at the meeting, saying inflation was tame and the strengthening mark should not be provoked.

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel upstaged the otherwise routine council meeting by traveling to Frankfurt to meet Bundesbank officials amid media reports saying the government was weighing plans to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves.

A Bonn finance ministry spokeswoman denied gold sales were planned but officials left open whether balance sheet moves could be used to help whip Germany's finances into shape for European currency union, prompting speculation that a move to change the bank's accounting practices might be on the cards.

German financial markets showed little reaction to the decision as Bund futures contracts for June delivery remained down about 35 basis points at 102.21 points and the 30-share DAX index was down 15.20 points at 3,558.49 points at midday.

All 10 economists surveyed by Reuters this week had said the central bank would keep rates on hold. Only one economist predicted a cut in the discount and Lombard rates this year while none predicted a rate rise during the rest of 1997.
Economists believe the German economy is showing signs of modest recovery and no danger of inflation, providing no reason for the Bundesbank to take action on rates in either direction.
